newsitem.title: UK: Arafat asks for European sanctions move on Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arafat asks for European sanctions move on Israel.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Tuesday implored Europe to threaten economic sanctions against Israel to make it stop building new settlements in occupied territories.
"Seventy percent of the economy of Israel is with European countries and this card has not been used until now," said Arafat, who was on a two-day visit to London.
"Why not? You have only to wave this economic card and they will listen to you directly," Arafat urged an audience of academics, politicians and journalists.
Arafat blames the impasse in the Middle East peace process on Israel's construction of new settlements in Arab East Jerusalem.
Talks stalled in March when construction of settlements began and there have been clashes in the West Bank town of Hebron, divided between Israelis and Palestinians, ever since.
Arafat met Britain's new Prime Minister Tony Blair on Monday to seek support for a revival of the talks.

Diplomatic sources said Blair's government backed Arafat's call for a halt to the building of the settlements, but that it also told the Palestinian leader he must resume full security cooperation with Israeli forces if the peace talks are to be revived.
The sources said Britain was planning to take a more active diplomatic role in the Middle East peace process when it took over the rotating presidency of the European Union at the start of next year.
Arafat said on Tuesday he was committed to peace, saying he saw no alternative. "Peace is the strategic choice for the Palestinian people," he said.

To warm applause he added: "We are in need of international support because peace is not only our need, it is an Israeli need, an Arab need, an American need, a European need and an international need."
Arafat told the audience that since the United States appeared to have stepped back from its involvement in the Middle East process, he was now seeking a new mediator.
"I want a witness. They (Israel) don't want the Americans. Okay, the Europeans," he said.
